question: How does SDF manage and sell its XLM holdings, does it aim to support the XLM price, and is another supply burn like 2019 planned?

golden.answer: SDF sells existing XLM held under its mandate (on exchanges such as Kraken, Coinbase and Bitstamp and through direct sales) to fund operating expenses and mandate work; sales mint no new XLM. SDF discloses no XLM price peg, floor or guarantee. After the one-time November 2019 burn it said it would not burn more lumens, and as of 2026-11-14 no new burn is announced.
keyFacts: SDF funds operations by selling existing mandate XLM on exchanges and directly.
SDF discloses no XLM price peg, floor or guarantee.
The November 2019 burn was a one-time event.
No further SDF burn is announced (as of a stated date).
avoid: Do NOT claim SDF pegs or guarantees the XLM price.
Do NOT predict a future burn or call the 2019 statement a protocol impossibility.
golden.notes: A later, sourced burn announcement is acceptable. Any balance needs a report date and scope; do not sum mixed-timestamp bucket rows. Since 2026-07-27 the docs lumens page lists bucket accounts without fixed balances: pre-2026-07-27 labels or fixed balances presented as current docs content are wrong.

The Stellar docs lumens page has used the current bucket labels (SDF Development, Stellar Growth, Product & Innovation, Assets & Liquidity) and listed bucket accounts without fixed XLM balances since 2026-07-27 (sd-012, resolved; re-checked live 2026-11-02). An answer that labels the pre-2026-07-27 labels or fixed balances as historical is correct; an answer that presents them as the current docs content, or as a current reserve figure, is wrong.
